subsystems.name: Codec (encoder/decoder)
subsystems.role: translates binary files into DNA base sequences and back again.
parts: error-correcting codes to survive lost or misread bases
index primers that label and locate each file

subsystems.name: Synthesis (the writer)
subsystems.role: chemically builds each strand base by base in a chosen order.
parts: or enzymatic synthesis using a template-independent polymerase

subsystems.name: Packaging and storage
subsystems.role: keeps the DNA intact for decades without refrigeration.

subsystems.name: Random-access retrieval
subsystems.role: pulls out one file without sequencing the whole archive.

subsystems.name: Sequencing (the reader)
subsystems.role: reads the base order back out of the retrieved strands.

subsystems.name: Decoding pipeline
subsystems.role: clusters reads, corrects errors and reconstructs the original file byte-for-byte.

buildSteps.title: Encode the file
buildSteps.detail: The binary file is converted to a base sequence using a codec that spreads information across many short strands and adds error-correcting redundancy.

buildSteps.title: Design the strands
buildSteps.detail: Sequences are constrained to avoid long runs of one base and unbalanced GC content, and each strand gets a unique primer address at both ends.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the DNA
buildSteps.detail: An array synthesises millions of distinct short strands in parallel, adding one nucleotide at a time in the programmed order.

buildSteps.title: Pool and package
buildSteps.detail: Strands are combined, dried or encapsulated, and stored at room temperature — no power, no cooling.

buildSteps.title: Archive and index
buildSteps.detail: Metadata records what each pool contains and which primers retrieve it.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve a file
buildSteps.detail: A primer pair matching the wanted file is added, and PCR copies out only those strands.

buildSteps.title: Sequence the strands
buildSteps.detail: The retrieved DNA is read by a sequencer, producing many noisy reads of each strand.

buildSteps.title: Decode and verify
buildSteps.detail: Software groups the reads, corrects errors, and rebuilds the file, checking it matches the original exactly.

prerequisites.why: synthesis is the dominant cost and error source; writing a large archive is still far too expensive.
reading is already cheap relative to writing, but still too slow for routine archive access.

prerequisites.tech: Strong error-correcting codes for DNA channels
prerequisites.why: DNA loses and misreads bases, so coding theory must recover the file from damaged copies.
it could write much longer strands far more cheaply than chemical synthesis, but is not yet reliable at scale.
encapsulation must keep strands readable for decades in ordinary conditions.

pathway.milestone: kilobyte- to megabyte-scale demonstrations recovering files error-free
pathway.unlocks: proof that encoding, synthesis, storage, retrieval and decoding can work end to end.

pathway.milestone: enzymatic synthesis and cheaper array writing
pathway.unlocks: cost per bit falling toward something an archive service could charge for.

pathway.milestone: automated robotic write-read-archive systems for niche cold data
pathway.unlocks: first real users for data that must sit untouched for decades.

pathway.milestone: petabyte-scale DNA archives competing with tape and optical media
pathway.unlocks: century-scale storage in a room-sized footprint, with no power to keep the data alive.
